findings.claim: The hero cue fires the first frame heroProp.radius <= voidling.radius * EAT_RATIO (1.11), heroProp being the single largest edible in the world resolved at match start. Thresholds: Maple 6.5 -> R 5.86; Pirate 10 -> 9.01; Game Day 11 -> 9.91; Lantern 11 -> 9.91; Powder 10.5 -> 9.46; Skylark 18 -> 16.22.
findings.evidence: if (heroProp && COPY.heroCue && !heroCued && !heroProp.mesh.userData.eaten && heroProp.radius <= voidling.radius * EAT_RATIO) (:10753-10754); heroProp = largest edible :6114-6116; EAT_RATIO = 1.11 :3673

findings.claim: Growth is clock-bound, not eat-bound: lawCap = min(12, 0.9 + (0.022*min(t,30) + 0.025*t)*paceK + surgeT^2*(2.8+2.6*pace)) + feastR, feastR = +1.25 per rival eaten (max +6). Without the finale surge the clock alone buys r 6.06 at 180 s ('the old 6.06 plateau'); the surge/pace term reaches ~14.5 on a strong run. So a radius-10/11 landmark is reachable only inside the finale surge — by design 'the last half-minute' — and Maple's 5.86 crosses at ~132 s of 180 on an optimal run (measured, qa/pace.mjs). No measured cue time exists for the other five worlds.
findings.evidence: LAW_TOP = 12 :9745; lawCap :9746-9748; FEAST_PER_RIVAL 1.25 :3689; 'Maple's radius is 4.85 at 120s and 6.09 at 140s, so it crosses at about t=132s' :1517-1520; 'topped out at 6.06 on a 3:00 clock' :9693; '~14.5 on a strong run' :9733; 'a radius-10 hotel that only becomes edible in the last half-minute' :1553-1555

findings.claim: SKYLARK's LANDMARK goal is impossibly late as authored: the whale needs R >= 16.22, and lawCap tops at 12 + feastR, so it requires at least 4 rivals eaten (12+5.0 >= 16.22; 12+3.75 does not) — plus the tether window. island.ts:6183-6186 claims 'an idle child at r7 can take an r18 meal', which contradicts the EAT_RATIO gate at :5879; which is true is unsure and must be measured, not argued.

constraints_for_the_build: The heroCue threshold is derived, not a separate constant: heroProp = largest edible, cue at heroProp.radius <= R * EAT_RATIO (prototype3d.ts:6114-6116, :10753). A LANDMARK level must reuse heroProp and heroAte/byPlayer (:10768-10775), not a second list.

Growth is clock-bound (lawCap :9746-9748, LAW_TOP 12). A LANDMARK level that 'wins on the spot' on a 10-11 radius landmark is decided by the finale surge timing, not by eating; do not tune N against it without qa/pace.mjs radius-vs-time per world (only Maple is measured: 5.86 at ~132 s).

Skylark's whale is tethered (island.ts:6196; eat gate :5597,:5879) and needs R >= 16.22 (> LAW_TOP 12 without >= 4 rivals eaten). Either the goal names a different Skylark landmark (tower 4.2 :6448, hangars 5.5 :6499) or the whale's edible radius/tether changes; measure first.
questEvent('big') double-fires on tagged-big props with r >= 6 (:5826 + :5829); a SET counter must dedupe per bite before any N is honest.
'cabana' is a radius band 2.6-3.4 (:5828) — on Maple it counts sedans, on Lantern sheds. Use it as a SET kind on Pirate only, or retag.
Supply is shared with up to five rivals (family share of bites measured 40-50%, :523-525); keep 3N <= supply, and prefer N where 6N <= supply for cars/houses.
Powder has exactly one r>=6 prop (:3864-3866) and Skylark two house-tagged props (world6.verdict.md:99-100): 'big' on Powder and 'house' on Skylark are dead kinds.
Every per-world table must have six rows keyed by WorldId (the Record<WorldId,...> pattern at :1492) — the ternary fallthrough bug is recorded three times (:3843-3870, :3899-3906).
Maple has hero: null (:1501); a diorama needs an authored subject there — the town hall at 3D (42.75,-68) is the only r>=6 prop.

Static counts here are REQUESTED scatter counts (plant/scatterInRegion n); placement drops some (Game Day once placed 861 of 2,364 :6740-6744). Live counts come from qa/questable.mjs supply, which the gate already runs per world.
Skylark's poster path is remote-only (CDN refused from this container, :6636-6659); paintWorldCard keeps CARD_FALLBACK if it 404s.
cheapest_path: Level table as one Record<WorldId, LevelSpec[5]> next to WORLD_COPY (:1492) with EAT = 0.6*WORLD_PAR, SET kinds drawn from the existing MED/HARD_BY_WORLD-serviceable set (:3896-3907) with N from the questable supply, LANDMARK = existing heroProp/heroAte path (:6114, :10768), RIVALS = myRank at endMatch (:4737), CLEAR = devouredPct (:5339-5344). Before choosing any LANDMARK N or SET N, run qa/pace.mjs for all six worlds to get radius-vs-time and qa/questable.mjs supply per world (both already exist, no new probe needed for measurement); extend questable's supply dump to dedupe the 'big' double-fire. Diorama subject per world = COPY.hero (five worlds) and the town hall for Maple.
risks: LANDMARK on worlds 2-5 lands in the last ~30 s by growth-law design (:1553-1555); with 'clock runs out = fail' a slower child may never see the cue (Maple weak-run note :1529-1531) — a level that fails on pace rather than play.
Skylark LANDMARK as the whale is likely unreachable (R 16.22 vs LAW_TOP 12); the island.ts:6185 claim to the contrary is unverified.
Requested prop counts overstate live supply; Pirate's car (7) and big (12) and Lantern's big (5) are thin enough that rivals can eat the SET out.
'big' double-count and the 'cabana' radius band make two of the shipped kinds dishonest as SET counters.
Poster art is the diorama's competitor: five posters were painted 'no void in frame', a live diorama with the void in it changes the picker's visual contract (:6597-6612).
EAT = 0.6 par is a proposal from par arithmetic, not a measured clear-rate; polish plan bar 5 requires playtest measurement.

Should heroProp on Skylark be the whale at all, given the tether, or the tower/hangars?
